name: Mikneiah
overview: Mikneiah was a male Levite who held the important role of a gatekeeper, ranking second among the Levites in this capacity. His service is noted specifically in 1 Chronicles 15:18, highlighting his position in the temple duties during the time of David. As a Levite, he was part of the tribe set apart for religious service and temple responsibilities.
namesAndTitles: The name Mikneiah means "YHWH acquires," reflecting a theologically rich meaning that points to God's sovereign action in acquiring or taking possession. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:18, emphasizes the divine connection of his identity and role within Israel's worship life.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mikneiah as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the priestly tribe responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mikneiah's significance lies in his role as a second rank Levite gatekeeper, a position essential for maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple. His mention in 1 Chronicles 15:18 places him among those who facilitated the proper worship of God during a pivotal time in Israel's history, underscoring the importance of faithful service in God's house. Through his role, Mikneiah exemplifies the dedicated Levitical ministry that foreshadows Christ's priestly work.
